claims.claim: Opens with a preface written by Walter Hartright, drawing-master
claims.evidence: '(of Clement's Inn, Teacher of Drawing)'; 'the writer of these introductory lines (Walter Hartright by name)'

claims.claim: Story will be told by several witnesses
claims.evidence: 'the story here presented will be told by more than one pen'

claims.claim: On the last day of July he walks toward Hampstead
claims.evidence: 'It was the last day of July'; 'I turned my steps northward in the direction of Hampstead'

claims.claim: He meets a lone woman dressed all in white
claims.evidence: 'the figure of a solitary Woman, dressed from head to foot in white'

claims.claim: Anne Catherick escaped from an asylum
claims.evidence: 'She has escaped from my Asylum'

claims.claim: Walter teaches at Limmeridge, Marian is Laura's half-sister
claims.evidence: 'Limmeridge House'; 'my half-sister Laura'; 'My name is Marian Halcombe'

claims.claim: Laura is engaged to Sir Percival; Walter leaves
claims.evidence: Marriage settlement clauses re Sir Percival; Walter's departure (read from settlement/plot scenes)

claims.claim: Glyde and Fosco want Laura's money
claims.evidence: marriage-settlement £20,000 clause; 'in the case of Lady Glyde's death, what do...'

claims.claim: They have Anne die
claims.evidence: Anne died on 25 July 1850 'at No. 5 Forest Road'; death not shown as engineered
claims.fix: When Anne dies at Fosco's house, she is buried as Lady Glyde

claims.claim: declare her to be Laura, who is shut in an asylum
claims.evidence: 'Anne Catherick had been introduced into Count Fosco's house as Lady Glyde...Lady Glyde had taken the dead woman's place in the Asylum'
claims.fix: the dead woman is passed off as Lady Glyde, while Laura is shut in the asylum in Anne's place

claims.claim: Marian and Walter rescue Laura
claims.evidence: Lady Glyde taken from the Asylum; 'My wife and Marian were both upstairs'

claims.claim: Glyde is no baronet's legitimate son
claims.evidence: text shows forgery: 'there, at Old Welmingham, was the forgery committed in the register of the church'
claims.fix: Walter discovers that Glyde forged an entry in a church register

claims.claim: Glyde dies in a fire in the vestry
claims.evidence: 'purposely setting the vestry on fire'; 'the fire and the death'; 'Sir Percival's death'

claims.claim: Fosco killed in Paris by the Brotherhood
claims.evidence: 'taken out of the Seine'; 'The hand that struck him'; 'member of the Brotherhood'; Morgue

claims.claim: Walter marries Laura; their son is heir
claims.evidence: 'when our little Walter was six months old'; 'Mr. Walter Hartright—the Heir of Limmeridge'

claims.claim: Mr. Fairlie is Laura's uncle
claims.evidence: 'My uncle, Mr. Fairlie'; 'Mr. Fairlie's invalid condition'

claims.claim: Pesca is Walter's Italian friend
claims.evidence: 'my worthy Italian friend, Professor Pesca'

claims.claim: Anne looks like Laura
claims.evidence: 'the personal resemblance between the woman in white and Lady Glyde'

claims.claim: Sir Percival is a baronet
claims.evidence: 'one Baronet that you don't...'; 'baronet, the possessor of a fine estate'

claims.claim: Fosco is fat
claims.evidence: 'Count Fosco, as fat as Henry the...'
